note: Extraction, verification, retrieval and abstention code frozen BEFORE the test split's candidate sheets were generated or read. Any later change to these files invalidates the test numbers.

why: retrieval: opt-in retrieval.rarity_unit='papers' (default 'findings' = frozen behaviour); one big meta-analysis made its drug look common and let 2 wrong-drug answers through on test
verification: '%-' is a range separator, not a minus sign (1 false provenance rejection on test)
verification+extraction: scientific-notation p-values ('1.02 x 10-6' was read as p=1.02; 2 wrong p-values on test)
evaluation: run_queries(exclude=...) to drop one audited query-label error
post_hoc.test_status: Numbers in data/m1/results/ come from the frozen snapshot (data/m1/frozen_snapshot/) and are the held-out result. Numbers in data/m1/results_posthoc/ use the changed code + configs/posthoc.toml and are NOT held-out (the changes were motivated by test failures).
post_hoc.intermediate_state_note: The source exactly as it stood when the first post-hoc run was made (recorded earlier as 25f6d4df...) was not preserved and no hash of it can be re-verified; the two states that ARE preserved and hash-verified are frozen_snapshot (test freeze) and frozen_snapshot_fresh (held-out fresh predictions).

fresh_holdout.note: System predictions on the 55 fresh papers (+6 agreement papers) were generated and hashed BEFORE any independent annotation of them existed. The fresh papers were never seen during development.
fresh_holdout.regenerate: PYTHONPATH=data/m1/frozen_snapshot_fresh/src python scripts/predict_papers.py --map data/m1/independent/pack/blind_map.json --raw-fresh data/raw/fresh --raw-main data/raw/pmc --config data/m1/frozen_snapshot_fresh/configs/default.toml --out OUT.jsonl  # byte-identical to predictions_file

fetch_manifest_note: sha256 of data/raw/pmc/manifest.jsonl, the discovery fetch's own output (git-ignored, 111 rows); it is NOT the committed data/m1/corpus_manifest.jsonl, which has the same PMCIDs plus per-file sha256/bytes columns added by the pinning step, so it cannot be verified from the repo
hash_algorithms: tree hash = sha256 over each file under the directory in ascending POSIX relative path order: the path as UTF-8, then the bytes (__pycache__ excluded); file hash = sha256 of the bytes. Recompute everything with scripts/verify_freeze.py

post_review.what: Changes made AFTER the independent annotation and the red-team review. NOT held-out for anything they were motivated by.
why: extraction: credible intervals, LSMD, Cohen d/Hedges g, 'absolute difference in risk', number-inside-filler, DOI and within-arm guards, sign loss after a filler (independent annotation)
extraction: scientific-notation p-values (3.1e-4, 1.2 x 10^-5, P<10-4), Lancet middle-dot decimals, heart-rate / RR-interval guards, 6000-character sentence cap (red-team review)
verification: positional 'estimate_reproduced' check, hash recomputed from the text, e-notation numbers (red-team review)
ids: finding_id includes the interval and is unique per document; restatements collapse across sentences only (red-team review)
evaluation: AURC over answered queries only; field F1 ignores None/None pairs (red-team review)
conflicts: 'p<0.05' counts as significant; differing units / MD vs SMD are not compared (red-team review)
post_review.results: data/m1/results_postreview/ (dev + test, current code + configs/posthoc.toml) and data/m1/independent/scores_postreview_lenient/

pinned_files.algorithm: file hash (sha256 of bytes); paths relative to data/m1/

limits_of_this_record: Hashes show that a file is unchanged since this record was written. They cannot show WHEN code or gold was frozen relative to the test annotation: the timestamps here are self-reported by the author, and the whole procedure was run by one party.
